title: Throne Hall of Dongola
representedDate: Standing mosque as documented after the 2015–2017 archaeological conservation, with its retained battered mass and rebuilt terrace parapet.
geometryBasis: Native standing ruin outline, with documented overall dimensions of approximately 28 m by 18 m by 12 m including the irregular masonry.
sectionBasis: The original Qualla engraving shows the batter, small upper openings and stair enclosure. University of Warsaw fieldwork describes the roughly 6.5 m ground storey, 3.1 m upper storey, western stair entry and post-conservation roof parapet.
limitations: Roof enclosure, aperture positions and wall batter are approximated from the published silhouette and archaeological descriptions. The surviving standing state follows the documented 2015–2017 conservation.
The model represents the exterior, including the restored terrace, without reconstructing the earlier Makurian palace state, buried rooms or surroundings.
